implication: Use to explain why dependence/heavy-use screening is part of onboarding and why high-risk users need medical advice.
caveat: Mechanistic plausibility is not direct evidence for the benefits or harms of a short-term challenge in low-risk users.

headline: A combined risk tool outperforms isolated symptoms for severe withdrawal prediction.
implication: Use to support structured screening and referral logic rather than relying on a single symptom or a user’s subjective confidence.
caveat: The review’s hospitalized setting and base rates may not apply directly to lower-risk community challengers.

headline: DT is potentially fatal without prompt adequate management.
implication: Use to justify hard-stop/urgent-care language for delirium, severe confusion, hallucinations, or prior DT history.
caveat: Does not provide benefit evidence for abstinence challenge variants.

headline: ASAM separates withdrawal management from AUD treatment and wellness challenges.
implication: Use as a core source for routing risky users to medical withdrawal management instead of self-directed abrupt cessation.
caveat: Do not treat ASAM withdrawal recommendations as instructions for users to medicate themselves.

headline: Even outpatient withdrawal management requires daily monitoring and risk triage.
implication: Use to distinguish a low-risk alcohol-free challenge from outpatient detoxification; anyone with AWS risk factors should not be routed into a simple challenge.
caveat: Outpatient management is not synonymous with unsupervised abstinence.

headline: High-risk drinking guidelines pair screening with withdrawal-management pathways.
implication: Use to support screening and referral language for high-risk drinking/AUD before short-term abstinence variants.
caveat: Does not show that a 7-, 14-, or 30-day alcohol-free challenge is effective or safe for dependent drinkers.

headline: Hospital AWS protocols show the level of monitoring required for active withdrawal.
implication: Use as practical safety-context evidence for escalation when users report withdrawal symptoms or high-risk history.
caveat: Do not adapt hospital medication protocols into user-facing self-treatment instructions.

headline: Hospital withdrawal management is a separate clinical pathway.
implication: Use as current context for hospital screening, assessment, and medication boundaries if users report high-risk symptoms or history.
caveat: The source is not direct evidence for any abstinence-challenge outcome.

headline: Medication-managed withdrawal is clinical care, not a self-directed challenge.
implication: Use to reinforce that high-risk withdrawal prevention/treatment belongs with clinicians, not protocol claims.
caveat: Older meta-analysis/guideline; do not use as the only modern treatment source.

headline: VA/DoD places alcohol withdrawal in stabilization and clinical-care pathways.
implication: Use to support clinician-guidance boundaries for users with dependence, severe symptoms, or complicated withdrawal history.
caveat: Do not copy guideline PDFs into Git unless rights are separately verified.

headline: SAWS can inform symptom logging but not safety clearance.
implication: Use only as context for optional symptom tracking after high-risk users have been screened out or referred.
caveat: Do not present a self-report score as permission to ignore severe symptoms or medical-risk history.

headline: Prior or possible withdrawal seizure risk is a hard safety boundary.
implication: Use to make history of withdrawal seizures or seizure-like events an exclusion/referral trigger before alcohol abstinence challenges.
caveat: Mechanistic evidence does not quantify seizure probability in low-risk users.

headline: Supervised home detox is adjacent care, not an alcohol-free challenge.
implication: Use only to separate supervised detoxification from wellness protocol participation.
caveat: Older sample and care model; do not use for broad modern safety claims.

headline: Anticonvulsant evidence is limited and not a self-treatment basis.
implication: Use to avoid overstating non-benzodiazepine seizure-prevention options in protocol safety language.
caveat: Mixed/limited medication evidence belongs in clinician care, not user-facing medication advice.

headline: SAWS validation supports symptom tracking only within safety boundaries.
implication: Use as optional measurement context after excluding/referring high-risk users, not as a clearance tool.
caveat: Self-reported symptoms can lag risk and should not override prior seizure/DT/dependence history.

headline: Magnesium evidence is insufficient for AWS treatment or prevention.
implication: Use to avoid unsupported supplement claims during alcohol-free challenges, especially for users at withdrawal risk.
caveat: Do not infer that magnesium prevents withdrawal complications.

headline: Outpatient withdrawal care is still clinical care.
implication: Use to distinguish low-risk alcohol-free challenge participation from outpatient detoxification and referral needs.
caveat: Should not be used to encourage unsupervised withdrawal in dependent drinkers.

headline: Community detox evidence supports supervised care boundaries, not protocol efficacy.
implication: Use to route users needing detoxification toward care models rather than a wellness abstinence challenge.
caveat: Do not promote community-detox findings as evidence that unsupervised challenges are safe.

headline: Selected outpatient detox can be lower cost, but it is still medical detox.
implication: Use to avoid conflating outpatient detoxification with self-directed alcohol-free challenge variants.
caveat: Cost and safety results are not a clearance rule for unsupervised withdrawal.

headline: Baclofen evidence is insufficient for AWS management conclusions.
implication: Use to prevent overgeneralized claims about alternative medications during alcohol-free challenges.
caveat: The finding does not address baclofen for AUD relapse prevention outside AWS and should not be broadened.

headline: Long-term heavy use requires screening before abrupt abstinence.
implication: Use to explain why the challenge needs pre-screening for dependence, prior withdrawal, and need for clinician-guided withdrawal management.
caveat: Do not cite as proof of wearable or biomarker benefit from abstinence.

headline: Ambulatory withdrawal still requires appropriate support.
implication: Use to state that people with withdrawal risk need supported care pathways rather than simple challenge enrollment.
caveat: Guideline overview should not be used to define all eligibility thresholds alone.

headline: AWS hospitalizations are a population-level safety burden tied to high-risk drinking signals.
implication: Use as observational context for why alcohol-screening questions matter before short-term abstinence variants.
caveat: Do not infer that an individual challenge causes or prevents hospitalization from this cohort.
